decisions.title: Release rule A: ship if better than live
decisions.words: A, B, and C together please.
decisions.where: critic/RUBRIC.md §3; critic/policy.json release block; shipVerdict and validateReport in tools/critic-policy.mjs; tests/unit/critic-release-rules.test.ts. A build deploys when its reviewed changed area has no critical defect introduced or left reachable by the change and no regression against the live build; majors that are not regressions are disclosed in the release announcement and carried into the next batch; defects inside a brand-new feature do not block, and that feature may ship switched off; unknown on a critical is a HOLD. Asked after two candidates in a row were held for a day by the pre-deploy deep review although each was better than the live build.

decisions.title: Release rule B: the deep review runs after the deploy
decisions.words: A, B, and C together please.
decisions.where: critic/RUBRIC.md §4; critic/policy.json release.deepBeforeDeployClasses and release.maxDeploysWithDeepOwed; tools/critic-plan.mjs, tools/deploy-pages.mjs, critic/runner/release.js. A shared-system change needs a focused review of the production candidate before the deploy and its deep review afterwards on the live build, where it stays that build's obligation and its issue list drives the next batch. Deep-before-deploy survives only for the save-data class (src/app/SaveData.ts, save schema or migration) and a milestone claim; at most two deploys may go out while a deep review is owed, the third refuses. The finished-milestone standard is unchanged.
